title: signing.rs: temp key file created world-readable before chmod
description:
## Why this issue exists

In crates/core/src/signing.rs, write_signing_key() creates a temp file with File::create(), then calls set_permissions(0o600) on it, then writes key material, then renames into place.

File::create() creates with mode controlled by process umask. Under a permissive umask (0o022, the Linux default), the file exists as 0o644 (world-readable) between creation and set_permissions. Another process reading the directory during that window can read the private key.

## What breaks

Ed25519 operator private key is exposed world-readable for a brief window during key generation or rotation. On multi-user systems this is a credential-leak.

## Fix direction

Use OpenOptions with mode(0o600) at creation time via std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt so the file is never created with broader permissions. Or use tempfile::NamedTempFile which uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL with 0o600, then persist and rename.
